best_for: Bedroom and club DJs on a budget who want a full four-deck setup with controller and timecode vinyl support, without a paid upgrade waiting behind the free version.
description:
Mixxx is DJ software made by the Mixxx Development Team, a volunteer project that has been building it since 2001.

Turn on Sync Lock and your decks stay in time even when you change the speed, so you can stack tracks and loops into a live remix. Auto DJ crossfades a playlist for you when you need a break, and ReplayGain keeps the loudness of each song even. Four microphone and four auxiliary inputs let a singer or guitar join the mix without an outside mixer. Build crates and playlists to plan a set, and fill in missing tags from MusicBrainz by fingerprinting your tracks. If you like to tinker, you can write your own controller mappings in JavaScript.

points.title: The full version is the free one
points.text: Mixxx is GPL-licensed and has no paid or pro edition. What you download is everything. Donations go through Open Collective and are optional.

points.title: Four decks and 64 samplers
points.text: You get four decks with waveforms, hotcues, beat loops and keylock, up to 64 sampler decks, and effect chains of up to three effects each. BPM and key are detected, and the library sorts by both.

points.title: Controllers and timecode vinyl
points.text: Mappings ship for many controllers, such as the Pioneer DDJ-SB2, Numark Mixtrack Pro 3 and Allen & Heath Xone K2. Timecode vinyl control with turntables or CDJs is included at no cost, which other DJ apps often sell as an add-on.

points.title: Brings your existing library
points.text: Mixxx can read libraries from iTunes, Traktor, Rekordbox, Serato, Rhythmbox and Banshee. The features page names no streaming-service integration, so plan on playing your own files.

points.title: Broadcast and record
points.text: Mixes can stream live to Shoutcast or Icecast servers and record to WAV, FLAC or Ogg Vorbis. MP3 recording needs the separate LAME library.

points.title: System needs and Linux routes
points.text: Windows needs 64-bit Windows 10 version 1809 or later, and the Mac build needs macOS 11 or later, in separate Intel and Apple silicon downloads. On Linux the project points to its Ubuntu PPA, RPM Fusion or Arch; it marks the Flatpak as unmaintained.

points.title: Stay on stable for gigs
points.text: The 2.6 beta snapshots carry a warning not to use them live. The Windows listing here keeps 7 versions; macOS lists only the current release, so Mac downgrades need another source.
